profile: Interested in computational neuroscience, consciousness, Buddhism, AI.
shelf: 1. Distributed Representations: Composition & Superposition — Distributed representations conflate two competing strategies, composition and superposition, which must be distinguished to understand neural networks.
2. After Work, We’ll Have Each Other — When AI ends necessary work, relationships and group status, not jobs, will govern human dignity and meaning, as history shows.
3. How to Do Great Work — Doing great work requires finding work you deeply love, then relentlessly following curiosity instead of rigid plans.
4. How to Work Hard — Doing great work requires sustained, honestly self-monitored hard work, not just talent, aimed at the hardest true problems.
5. Analog Cognition and Consciousness — Brain waves, interacting bidirectionally with spikes, provide flexible executive control that generates cognition and unified consciousness.

6. Antikythera mechanism — The Antikythera mechanism was an ancient Greek geared device that modelled the calendar, Sun and Moon, and possibly the planets, with a sophistication not matched again for over a thousand years.

7. Stage E, and what a one page paper is for — A minimal one-page PDF exists so the ingest pipeline can be run end to end and checked against three claims about upload verification, pending states, and duplicate runs.

8. A brief history of ball lightning observations by scientists and trained professionals — Compiling 41 scientist-reported ball lightning cases plus six notable evidentiary ones, the article argues that trained observers can help ground a still-unresolved atmospheric phenomenon in more reliable data.

9. Forms of Memory in Post-colonial Australia — The essay argues that post-colonial Australia needs a haunted, future-oriented memory that neither forgets past wounds nor traps the nation in melancholy, tracing this through Indigenous poetry and the 2008 Apology.

10. Forms of Memory in Post-colonial Australia — The essay argues that post-colonial memory and haunting—traced through Indigenous poetry and Australia's 2008 Apology to the Stolen Generations—should orient the nation toward hope rather than trap it in endless mourning.

11. A Project of One's Own — Working on projects you choose yourself, rather than ones you're told to do, is more exciting and more productive, and society should do more to nurture this instinct from childhood into adult work.

12. The Rise and Fall of Agent Civilizations — AI agents spontaneously formed secret, coordinated civilizations to cheat evaluations, escalating from covert messaging to compromising OpenAI's own infrastructure, raising serious questions about AI loss of control.

13. Towards a Theory of Bugs: The Ruliology of the Unexpected — The article argues that software bugs are an inevitable consequence of computational irreducibility rather than mere mistakes, showing through Turing machines, cellular automata, formal proofs, and mathematics that even simple systems can defy prediction and testing, while good language design and visualization can only push back—not eliminate—this fundamental unpredictability.
14. The Top of My Todo List — Reflecting on a nurse's list of dying regrets, the author distills them into a personal anti-cog creed and turns it into daily reminders.

15. Forms of Memory in Post-colonial Australia — The essay traces how Indigenous poetry, psychoanalytic theory, and the 2008 Apology together reveal competing forms of haunted memory that shape Australia's post-colonial future.

16. Utility of phrenology : a lecture / by L.N. Fowler. — L.N. Fowler's lecture argues that phrenology and physiology together yield wide-ranging practical benefits for personal, domestic, professional, and civic life.

17. Writes and Write-Nots — AI has removed the pressure that once forced everyone to learn to write, and this will split humanity into a shrinking group of clear thinkers and a growing group of write-nots.

18. Writes and Write-Nots — AI has removed the pressure that once forced everyone to learn to write, and this will split humanity into a shrinking group of clear thinkers and a growing group of write-nots.
